method: credential_test.sh (ffprobe/RTSP DESCRIBE variant) against standard default/weak/blank credential list

scope_tested.rtsp_note: non-standard port; default 554 not in use

control_probe.purpose: distinguish genuine weak-credential finding from a no-auth-enforced finding

result: All 6 standard default/weak/blank credential pairs rejected with RTSP 401 Unauthorized. Control probe (garbage credentials) also correctly rejected. No HTTP/HTTPS/SSH/Telnet admin interface exposed.

findings.issue: No standard default/weak/blank credentials accepted on any exposed local surface. RTSP on TCP/8554 correctly enforces authentication against this credential set.

methodology_note: Initial testing used curl for RTSP probing and produced a false-positive 100% success rate (first via OPTIONS, which is unauthenticated by spec on virtually all RTSP servers; then via DESCRIBE, where curl's RTSP engine was independently found to misreport server auth status). Switched to ffprobe (FFmpeg's RTSP client) after cross-checking a single request against both tools and finding curl reported 200 while ffprobe correctly reported 401 for the same URL with no credentials. ffprobe result is the authoritative one reported here.
notes: This is a valid null result for the standard default-credential attack surface, not an absence of findings — see CAM-S1-CRED-002 for the device-specific local RTSP credential finding that this test's wordlist-based approach could not have found.
